title: Project Overview
description: Start with README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md to understand what Rust Hover Preview does and how the runtime threads cooperate. These documents map the purpose, supported formats, and high-level source layout before touching code.

title: Application Entry Point
description: src/main.rs bootstraps the binary crate: it wires config, paths, and the module tree, then hands off to the app layer. Reading it first reveals the runtime structure a newcomer needs.
languageLesson: Rust binaries start at fn main(); the crate root declares modules with mod so downstream code can use paths like crate::app.

title: Core Application Modules
description: The app module handles startup, dialogs, single-instance enforcement, AFK handling, and updates. These routines coordinate the lifecycle touched in Step 2 and gate whether the hook and UI run.
languageLesson: mod.rs files act as module entry points, re-exporting child modules to keep use crate::app paths stable.

title: Configuration and Settings
description: Configuration persists settings, scales, and extension lists used across the app and UI. config.rs has high fan-in, meaning most subsystems depend on these values.
languageLesson: Rust config modules often centralize mutation behind a shared type; callers borrow the config instead of global state.

title: Format Detection and Routing
description: The formats module detects content type, parses file heads, and routes a file to the right reader or engine. It is a narrow layer with wide fan-in, so many readers depend on its decisions.

title: Format-Specific Readers
description: Readers implement parsing for archives, images, fonts, video, PDF, and Office content. The reader cluster shares a mod entry point, so new formats plug in by adding a reader and registering it in routing.

title: Rendering Engines
description: Engines render heavier documents and media through WebView, ImageMagick, LibreOffice, Office, and a document cache. They bridge format detection to actual pixel or text output.

title: Shell Integration
description: Explorer hook and tray modules connect the app to Windows: the hook captures hover and keyboard input, while the tray exposes settings and updates. pin_navigation and key_input carry user intent into the UI.

title: Text and Audio Previews
description: Text processing prepares preview content, paints text, and supports archive and audio previews plus pin chrome. It connects format output to the panes the user actually sees.

title: Preview and Pin Windows
description: The UI layer renders the hover preview window and the pinned window with playback, chrome, and drag support. It is the final consumer of the format, reader, and text pipelines.

title: Build and Tooling
description: Cargo.toml declares dependencies and build profile, while CI workflows run tests and deploy. These define how the single crate is compiled and shipped.

title: Licensing and Contribution
description: README-adjacent documents such as CONTRIBUTING and PRIVACY explain how to contribute and what the app touches. They set expectations for privacy and maintenance without changing code.
